problems.title: Area from a hypotenuse median
problems.question: A right triangle has acute angle $15^\circ$ and median to the hypotenuse 0.6. Find its area.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: The hypotenuse is 1.2. Thus $S=1.2^2\sin30^\circ/4=1.44/8=0.18$.

problems.title: Area on a square grid
problems.question: Find the triangle area in the diagram, where one grid cell has area $2\text{ cm}^2$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: In grid coordinates read $B=(1,2),A=(6,1),C=(7,5)$. Then $BA=(5,-1)$ and $BC=(6,3)$.
The area is $|15+6|/2=10.5$ cells. Multiply by 2 to obtain $21\text{ cm}^2$.

problems.title: Check the printed similarity condition
problems.question: In trapezoid $ABCD$, $BC\parallel AD$, $ABC=ACD$, $AB=4,AC=6$, and $[ABC]=3.6$. Find $[ACD]$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
formulas: $[ABC]=AB\cdot AC\sin A/2$; cosine rule; similar-triangle areas have the square of the side ratio.
steps: Put $\alpha=BAC$. The area gives $\sin\alpha=0.3$, so $\cos\alpha=\pm\sqrt{91}/10$. Thus $BC^2=52\mp(24/5)\sqrt{91}$.
The printed angle equality and the parallel bases make $ABC\sim DCA$, with $BC$ corresponding to $CA$. Hence $[ACD]=3.6(6/BC)^2=129.6/[52\mp(24/5)\sqrt{91}]$.
Both choices of the sign can form a convex trapezoid (one has the longer base above). Neither area matches a printed numerical choice.
problems.note: The printed conditions do not determine a unique area, and neither resulting value matches a listed choice. Both acute and obtuse possibilities for angle BAC are retained; no changed angle condition is assumed.

problems.title: Triangle formed by three circle centres
problems.question: Two externally touching radius-3 circles both touch a radius-8 circle internally. Find the area of the centres’ triangle.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
formulas: External centre distance $=r_1+r_2$; internal centre distance $=R-r$.
steps: The triangle sides are $6,5,5$. The altitude to side 6 is $\sqrt{5^2-3^2}=4$.
The area is $6\cdot4/2=12$.

problems.title: Tangent segments determine the sides
problems.question: An incircle touches $AB$ at $M$, with $AM=3,BM=5,BC=7$. Find triangle area.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
formulas: Tangents from a common point are equal; Heron: $S=\sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}$.
steps: The two tangent lengths from $C$ are $7-5=2$. Hence $AC=3+2=5$ and $AB=8$.
The semiperimeter is 10. Thus $S=\sqrt{10\cdot3\cdot5\cdot2}=10\sqrt3$.

problems.title: Two altitudes add to a given length
problems.question: Sides 18 and 15 have altitudes whose sum is 22. Find the area.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: Therefore $S=90$.

problems.title: An incenter on an isosceles altitude
problems.question: The incenter divides the altitude to the base into segments 3 and 5. Find the triangle area.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
formulas: $S=rs$; in an isosceles triangle with height $h$ and half-base $x$, $S=hx$, $s=x+\sqrt{x^2+h^2}$.
steps: The height is 8. The inradius is the lower altitude segment. It must be less than $h/2$, since $r=hx/(x+\sqrt{x^2+h^2})<h/2$. Thus $r=3$.
Now $8x=3(x+\sqrt{x^2+64})$, so $\sqrt{x^2+64}=5x/3$. Squaring yields $x=6$.
The area is $8\cdot6=48$.

problems.title: Opposite triangles in a parallelogram
problems.question: An interior point is joined to all four vertices. Find the sum of the two opposite shaded triangles when the parallelogram area is $s$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: The shaded triangles have equal-length parallel bases. Their heights sum to the full parallelogram height.
Their total is therefore half the parallelogram area.

problems.title: The other leg of a trapezoid
problems.question: $BC\parallel AD$, $\cos BAD=1/7$, $AB=5,BC=9,AD=16$. Find $CD$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: The horizontal projection of $AB$ is $5/7$, and $h^2=25(1-1/49)=1200/49$.
The horizontal projection of $CD$ has length $16-9-5/7=44/7$. Thus $CD^2=(1200+1936)/49=64$.

problems.title: Equal inscribed angles give equal chords
problems.question: A cyclic quadrilateral has circumradius $2\sqrt3$, $BD=6$, and $BAC=CAD$. Which listed length can $CD$ have?
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
formulas: Equal inscribed angles subtend equal chords; chord length $=2R\sin(\theta/2)$.
steps: The angle condition gives $BC=CD$, so $C$ is a midpoint of an arc $BD$. Since $BD/(2R)=\sqrt3/2$, the minor central angle $BOD$ is $120^\circ$.
If $C$ is the midpoint of the minor arc, $CD=2R\sin30^\circ=2\sqrt3$. This is a printed choice.
problems.note: If C is instead on the other arc, CD=6 is also geometrically possible. The wording asks which listed value can occur, so it does not require a unique length from the conditions alone.

problems.title: Excluded inputs of a nested fraction
problems.question: Find the sum of values excluded from $1/(x-2/(x-1))$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
formulas: Every denominator must be defined and nonzero.
steps: The inner denominator excludes $x=1$. The outer denominator vanishes when $x(x-1)-2=0$, or $(x-2)(x+1)=0$.
The excluded values are $1,2,-1$, whose sum is 2.

problems.title: A parabola vertex equally far from both axes
problems.question: Find the smallest $a$ for which the vertex of $y=x^2-4ax+5a^2-3$ is equally far from the axes.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: Require $|2a|=|a^2-3|$. Equivalently $a^2-3=2a$ or $a^2-3=-2a$.
The solutions are $3,-1,1,-3$. The smallest is $-3$.

problems.title: Minimum on a restricted interval
problems.question: The minimum of $x^2-2x+4a-3$ on $[-3,0]$ is 13. Find $a$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: The vertex is at 1, to the right of the interval, so the function decreases throughout $[-3,0]$. Its minimum occurs at 0.
Thus $4a-3=13$, giving $a=4$.

problems.title: Radicals in denominators
problems.question: Find the domain of $1/\sqrt{6-7x-3x^2}+1/\sqrt{x+1}$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
formulas: Radicands in square-root denominators must be strictly positive.
steps: $6-7x-3x^2>0$ holds between its roots $-3$ and $2/3$. Also $x+1>0$, so $x>-1$.
Intersect these intervals.

problems.title: Integer roots larger than two
problems.question: $x^2+ax+b=0$ has integer roots both larger than 2. Which listed value can $a+b+1$ take?
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: Both factors are integers at least 2. Among $11,13,15,17,19$, only 15 is composite.
It is achievable: take $r=4,s=6$, giving $(r-1)(s-1)=3\cdot5=15$.

problems.title: Integer solutions after shifting the variable
problems.question: Find the sum of integer solutions of $|x^2+2x-1|\le|x+1|$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: The inequality becomes $|u^2-2|\le u$, or both $u^2-u-2\le0$ and $u^2+u-2\ge0$.
For $u\ge0$, these say $1\le u\le2$. Integer $t$ are $-2,-1,1,2$, so $x=-3,-2,0,1$. Their sum is $-4$.

problems.title: Maximize a quadratic expression
problems.question: $y+2x=6$. Find the maximum of $xy+4x-y$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: Substitute $y=6-2x$ to get $-2x^2+12x-6=-2(x-3)^2+12$.
The square is nonnegative, so the maximum is 12, attained at $x=3,y=0$.

problems.title: Range of a rational function
problems.question: Find the range of $(x^2-2)/(x^2+2)$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: Since $x^2+2\ge2$, the fraction $4/(x^2+2)$ takes every value in $(0,2]$.
Subtracting it from 1 gives $[-1,1)$. The lower endpoint occurs at 0; the upper endpoint is never reached.

problems.title: Factor by grouping
problems.question: Reduce $(9x^3+3x^2+3x+1)/(3x^2-2x-1)$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: Cancel $3x+1$, retaining the original exclusions $x\ne-1/3,1$.

problems.title: Integers strictly between two roots
problems.question: How many integers lie between the smallest and largest roots of $x^2+6x+|x+3|=6$?
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: $t^2+t-15=0$ gives the positive value $t=(\sqrt{61}-1)/2$, between 3 and 4.
The two roots $x=-3\pm t$ lie respectively in $(-7,-6)$ and $(0,1)$. Integers strictly between are $-6,-5,-4,-3,-2,-1,0$.

problems.title: A rational inequality
problems.question: Solve $14/(2x-1)>x-2$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: Critical points are $-3/2,1/2,4$. The numerator zeros are excluded by strictness; $1/2$ is undefined.
The signs on the four intervals are positive, negative, positive, negative. Keep the positive intervals.

problems.title: Exactly one graph intersection
problems.question: For how many real $a$ do $y=x^2+ax+a+2$ and $y=(1-a)x^2-2x$ have exactly one common point?
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: For $a=0$, this is the linear equation $2x+2=0$, giving one point.
For $a\ne0$, require discriminant zero: $(a+2)^2-4a(a+2)=(a+2)(2-3a)=0$. This gives $a=-2,2/3$.
Together there are three parameter values.

problems.title: A midpoint test for concavity
problems.question: For $f(x)=ax^2+bx+c$, $f(1)+f(3)<2f(2)$. What must be true?
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: Expand the three values; the $b,c$ terms cancel and the squared terms leave $2a$.
The inequality therefore gives $2a<0$.

problems.title: A symmetric expression of quadratic roots
problems.question: $x_1,x_2$ solve $x^2-\sqrt2x-\sqrt2=0$. Evaluate $(x_1-1)/(x_1+1)+(x_2-1)/(x_2+1)$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: The reciprocal sum is $(S+2)/(P+S+1)=\sqrt2+2$, since the denominator equals 1.
The requested value is $2-2(\sqrt2+2)=-2-2\sqrt2$.

problems.title: A sign inequality with an absolute factor
problems.question: Solve $(x^2-x-2)|x-1|/(x^2-3x+2)<0$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: Exclude $x=1,2$ and cancel $x-2$. The expression is $(x+1)|x-1|/(x-1)$.
For $x<1$, it is $-(x+1)$, negative exactly for $x>-1$. For $x>1$, it is $x+1>0$.
